citations.review_text:
Black Myth: Wukong is one of the best-looking games in modern gaming. That's just a fact!

I had been waiting for this release for many years, and it turned out to be amazing. The combat, visuals, and sound design are all amazing. There isn't much dialogue in this game, but what little dialogue there is has a very good English dub and is easy to understand. I really like the quirky, animal-like characters the monkey encounters throughout the game, especially the tiger blacksmith.

Even though many boss fights are repetitive or don't really feel worthy of being called boss fights and are more like mini-bosses, there are still a lot of very entertaining ones, especially in the first two chapters. Every visual element in the interface and menus is incredibly artistic, in the best possible way. I really like the fast travel system, skill tree, potion system, and bestiary.

The portraits of characters and enemies in the bestiary are presented in the best possible way for Wukong, as their artwork resembles traditional Chinese scroll paintings, often accompanied by a little poetry that has been localized as well as possible.

Some people criticize the corridor-like level design, but I actually preferred it over the more open maps in Chapters 2, 3, and 6. When I played Wukong at release, there was no map, which, as far as I know, has since been added and also looks very artistic, resembling an old Chinese painting.

I think I only experienced about 2–3 game crashes. One happened in the middle of the final boss fight of Chapter 2, and another occurred right after beating the final boss, which was pretty annoying since I had to beat him again.

The music is mostly ambient, but there are also some fitting battle themes that are truly worthy of the opponents they accompany, featuring traditional Chinese instruments.

However, there are also some criticisms of Wukong that I want to mention:
1. Hidden bosses and questlines that are not easy to figure out by yourself (most dragons…

A very good mix of combat and spell casting, with some Souls-like inspired features. The bosses aren't just HP bars but are well-thought-out transformations that can cancel your damage and make you mad. However, this gives the game the opportunity to showcase many very impressive boss fights. I was impressed by the Chinese and English VAs. Very good performances from the whole cast with memorable characters that leave an impression on the player. 

I had some visual issues and experienced about four crashes to the desktop during my 68 hours. I finished my first playthrough in 53 hours. The New Game Plus was a nice cleanup run. 

Overall, a 9/10 game. I will look out for the next game.

Ahhh, so glad that i could finally got to play this game. The game itself isn't that hard, it has some difficult encounters though if you want to 100%, but overall is easy enough. i have to say that i had some crashes along the way maybe at the time you are reading this the game got optimised better than i post this, but expect some crashes at worst times. Story was good and i can say that i wait for the next game happly and who knows, maybe i pay the full price :D

citations.review_text:
本来早早就预购了，结果等到影之刃零都要发售了，才开始玩黑神话

---

总体来看，这部作品显然远非完美，但处处可以看出是制作组的呕心沥血之作

黑神话在视觉上是超一流水准，场景、服装、人物设计，动画短片，以及对UE5 Nanite等功能的使用。这些都毫无疑问凭一己之力证明了中国游戏的工业水准已经可以制作一流3A作品。场景设计尤为突出，做到了中国水墨画中山林的意境，在一众UE5奇幻风作品有辨识度。

不过，在游戏性上，仍然有细节上的不足。导致这一缺点的原因，除了经验不足外，我认为也是设计策略选择了视觉优先。游戏科学太希望讲好他们的西游故事了，将西游的视觉和叙事元素放在游戏性之前。

首当其冲的是随处可见的空气墙。许多看上去可以走过去的地方，实际上不能通行。这就是设计者为了场景好看，而不舍得放置过多的障碍，让玩家一看就知道不该往那里走。三番五次地被空气墙劝返，就打击了玩家探索的积极性。虽然说这游戏不是开放世界（这一点也是玩了后才知道的嘛），但是保持玩家探索积极性仍然相当重要，因为这游戏藏有出奇多的隐藏剧情和地图。

动作系统设计上，能感觉出设计者有野心，天命人用棍战斗有其他用刀剑战斗的游戏完全不同的节奏和手感。也有努力加入目前主流动作游戏中看不到的机制，例如切手技。经过一段时间的适应，开始掌握这个动作系统的节奏之后，还是能打出几场爽快的战斗。但是，战斗系统和boss的对应设计还远未充分挖掘。技能虽然多，但是大多数基本没差别。中后期很多boss也不需要仔细思考。能称得上发挥了动作系统设计的酣畅淋漓的boss战也只有最后大圣残躯。二郎神都不算，他更多的是耍帅演出。大圣残躯是设计得很出色的boss战，也是动作游戏中经典的Mirror Boss（镜像型）。他像玩家一样行动，灵活地使用着那丰富的技能库，让人产生一种**原来这些能力在真正的大圣手里应该这么用**的感觉。这样就通过战斗设计，完成了叙事的最后一块拼图：传承大圣的遗志。

[I]Black Myth Wukong[/I] is a fantastically detailed standout. A western audience is aware of the broad strokes of Journey to the West - certainly so for Wukong himself - but the deeper intricacies and stroylines are a highlight of this game, wrapped in quality production.

[I]Black Myth Wukong[/I] concerns the experience of a monkey that is attempting to become Wukong, through his own westward journey. He retreads location and events throughout the story, meeting familiar characters and experiencing much of that which Wukong did. The game is certainly better if played by someone who had read the Journey to the West, but Black Myth Wukong had the foresight to include a detailed beastary and lore glossary. These all take the form of narratives, some of them long and branching. It's an amazing treat to see this when so many other games fail to include this sort of material at all, much less in a literary fashion, much much less with something that is actually good on its own.

The inclusion of the excellent glossary, a somewhat unneeded but certainly appreciated bit of extra content, is a consequence of the maximalist design that Wukong has. It can't just be varied, it has to be deep. It has to be memorable, offer choice but also offer consequence. Level design is on some degree linear with only one correct path, but that doesn't preclude the inclusion of multiple other options. Some of them might be dead ends, others offer treasure, but the point of it all is the grounding, the development of atmosphere. Wukong has no map. You must navigate these caves by learning the nature of the locations you see. It requires effort, but Wukong rewards this by providing something worth remembering. Are you really gonna use many, or even some of those 72 transformations that the game offers? Certainly not, most of them are entirely overshadowed by others. But the game lets you nevertheless.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that missing side quests can leave players under-leveled and struggling against bosses.

citations.review_text:
[h1] Awe inspiring from start to finish [/h1]

After hearing about the hype surrounding this game since its release, I got it as soon as I heard it's on sale (for the third time) Surprisingly, it lived up to expectations.

The combat style is your typical modern souls-like, it felt pretty similar to me as I came from stellar blade. The levelling and progression felt good, you're always very close to the next progression path during my playthrough. I liked the idea of different armours, but you kinda just get the one with the most defense and run that until you find a better one. it's good in concept.

The narrative absolutely gripped me from start to finish. the grandness in scope reminds me a lot of God of War 2. From [spoiler] fighting gods on top of clouds to running away from a den of spiders. [/spoiler] the scenery and spectacle of it all is absolutely mesmerising A standout moment is definitely the opening scene. I won't spoil it for anyone wanting to give it a go. 

The story pacing can be hit or miss, as it largely depends on if you like to do side quests. If you are a person that goes from main quest to main quest ignoring every side quest, you'll find yourself overwhelmed quite quickly as the game expects you to take your time, to explore, and to beat mobs on the way while exploring to give you exp. if you skip that, you are very likely under levelled and will fight a boss that is wayyyyy too hard for you.

I played the game in Chinese audio, and by golly the voice acting absolutely took me away. I felt like I was the Chosen One with how immersive the dialogues and story beats are voiced.

The visuals and audio of this game are amazing, that being said, there are still graphics glitches especially in shadows even now, some 2 years after it's initial release. the framerate is also pretty terrible compared to it's contemporaries.

Speaking of issues with performance, I also kept experiencing dx12 crashes? Thankfully the game saves itself quite often so i did…

Great game so far, the graphics are very nice and some bosses can be pretty hard but its managble. only critique is that its pretty easy to miss out on really great side quests, the game doesnt do much in terms of directing you.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the lack of difficulty changing is a little meh.

citation.review_text: This game was absolutely fire. With the large amount of souls like games now played through I can say: the visuals were fantastic, gameplay also fire although each weapon having exactly the same combo was a little repetitive (apart from erlang's spear). Overall like a top 5, but if we are just looking at boss fights the Erlang boss fight by itself was probably like a top 1 (it was fire). the one con of this game. the lack of difficulty changing is a little meh. Compared to other souls like games it isn't too challenging. So this is probably one of the best if not the best first souls like for someone starting as it is linear and challenging enough if you are just starting and the visuals and story get you hooked quick.
